title: Generalized Lattice Model
body_html:
Generalized Lattice Model

Let \(W\) be a symplectic \(F\)-space and let \(B\) be a self-dual lattice function in \(W\). Set \[ b=B_0/B_{0+}. \] The symplectic form on \(W\) induces a finite-field symplectic form on \(b\), hence a finite Heisenberg group \(H(b)\) and an oscillator representation \(S(b)\).

The generalized lattice model \(S(B_0)\) of the oscillator representation consists of locally constant compactly supported functions \[ f:W\to S(b) \] with the covariance rule \[ f(a+w)=\psi((1/2)\langle w,a\rangle_W)\,\omega_b(a)f(w) \qquad a\in B_0. \] This model gives a splitting \(\xi_B\) of the metaplectic cover over the stabilizer of \(B_0\). Its restriction to the pro-unipotent subgroup is canonical. If \(B=B_{x,x'}\) is the tensor-product lattice function attached to \(x\in B(G)\) and \(x'\in B(G')\), then \(\xi_B\) restricts to the splitting \(\xi_{x,x'}\) used to compare \(K\)-types on the two sides of the dual pair.
